name: Hydroxypropyl tetrahydropyrantriol (Pro-Xylane)

lead: Pro-Xylane is the trade name of hydroxypropyl tetrahydropyrantriol, a sugar-derived (C-xyloside) ingredient from L'Oreal's research that appears in anti-aging creams and serums. It is described as a booster of glycosaminoglycans, the molecules that help skin hold water and structure.
Its appearance payoff is firmer, better-hydrated skin with softer-looking lines. Published human trials are small randomized studies of finished products that combine it with other actives.

paras: It is applied topically in day or night creams and serums, often alongside niacinamide, panthenol or plant extracts, and sometimes after procedures such as laser or micro-focused ultrasound. Studies run for weeks to months.
Topical cosmetic ingredient; the trials reviewed report no safety signal specific to it, though products contain many ingredients and individual skin reactions can occur.

angle.text: Pro-Xylane is applied in anti-aging products for firmness and elasticity. In trials it is part of regimens, often used after aesthetic procedures.

lead: Hydroxypropyl tetrahydropyrantriol, sold as Pro-Xylane, is a C-glycoside made from the sugar xylose and developed for anti-aging skincare.[1][2] It is described in the literature as a plant-derived biologically active compound and is used in topical products to target the skin's aging signs.[1][3]

Laboratory work reports that it reduces ultraviolet-induced senescence markers in skin cells,[4] and small randomized trials have tested products containing it in menopausal women and in people treated with micro-focused ultrasound or PicoWay laser.[3][5][6]

paras: Pro-Xylane is a C-glycoside, and synthesis in aqueous media was reported in 2009; recent papers describe enzyme-based routes to the optically pure (S)-form from D-xylose.[1][2][7]

A multicentre, evaluator-blinded randomized study tested a compensating skin care complex containing pro-xylane in menopausal women.[3] A 2025 split-face randomized trial in 50 patients (98 percent women) compared a blueberry extract and Pro-Xylane cream with standard moisturizer after micro-focused ultrasound, with a primary endpoint of Global Aesthetic Improvement Scale over 180 days; the intervention side improved significantly on that endpoint.[5] A 112-day randomized trial in 88 women found a regimen with Pro-Xylane, niacinamide and panthenol after PicoWay laser gave lower transepidermal water loss, higher hydration and less redness at 14 days compared with standard cream.[6] These are combination products, so effects cannot be attributed to Pro-Xylane alone.

A 2026 cell study in HaCaT keratinocytes reports Pro-Xylane alleviating UV-induced senescence via SGK1-mediated p21 ubiquitination.[4] A liposomal gel with a Pro-Xylane intermediate has been tested for wound healing.[8]
